🇳🇵 Nepal–Tibet Border Avalanche & Flood | 26 August 2026 A major ice–rock avalanche near the Nepal–Tibet border triggered a cascading hazard: a large glacier mass collapsed from high elevation, sending ice, rock and sediment into the Lhende Khola. The debris blocked the river and formed a temporary barrier lake, which then released a powerful downstream surge of muddy water, debris and boulders. 🌡️ Possible factors: glacier instability, melting ice, steep crevassed terrain, meltwater lubrication and possible seismic triggering. ⚠️ Some claims remain unconfirmed, so the exact trigger requires scientific investigation. 🌊 Avalanche → Debris Flow → River Blockage → Dam Breach → Flood #Nepal #NepalFlood #NepalLandslide #NepalAvalanche #NepalTibetBorder Himalayas HimalayanAvalanche Landslide GlacierCollapse GlacialLake BarrierLake FlashFlood DebrisFlow LhendeKhola Bhotekoshi ClimateChange GlacierMelt NaturalDisaster DisasterScience EarthScience 26August2026

Amid Nepal’s devastating floods, a heartbreaking video of a little boy carrying his younger sister has left social media in tears. With scratches visible on their faces, the young boy reportedly searches for their parents while holding tightly onto his little sister. He is just a child himself, yet in a moment of unimaginable disaster, he appears to be protecting the one person he still has. The powerful visuals have reminded many people of Grave of the Fireflies, the heartbreaking story of siblings Seita and Setsuko struggling to survive amid the de*struction of war. But this is not a movie. These are real children, facing a real disaster, searching for the people they love. Sometimes, the most painful images are the ones that need no words. Résultat : des villages rayés de la carte, des routes emportées, des infrastructures entières détruites à la frontière entre le Népal et le Tibet. Le bilan humain continue d'évoluer, et des centaines de personnes — dont de nombreux touristes étrangers — restent portées disparues à l'heure où j'enregistre cette vidéo. Mais ce qui m'a le plus marqué en enquêtant sur ce sujet, c'est que ce n'est pas un accident isolé. Le Népal traverse une série d'épreuves climatiques depuis plusieurs années : crues, glissements de terrain, fonte accélérée des glaciers... Video: Screams Heard As Part Of Nepal Mountain Crumbles Into River In Seconds The latest floods and landslides have killed at least 24 people and left 14 missing across several districts in Nepal n Nepal, two sets of videos from separate places have one thing in common -- each contains six seconds that are hard to watch. In that short time, a mountainside is seen giving way, and the people watching can be heard crying out as it happens. The first video was shot near Lete in Mustang District, following a fresh spell of floods and landslides on Sunday. It shows a large section of a mountain sliding into the Kali Gandaki River in the valley below within about six seconds. Residents can be heard screaming as the debris rushes downhill. The footage was recorded by Char Dham pilgrims. Rescuers search for 12 missing after Nepal avalanche kills two Rescue teams resume search for missing people after an avalanche on Himlung Himal killed two people during severe weather. Share Rescuers search for 12 missing after Nepal avalanche kills two on social media  Rescuers are searching for a dozen people swept away by an avalanche that killed at least two others on a Nepalese mountain during severe weather. At least 10 people have been rescued from Mount Himlung, a 7,126-metre (23,380-foot) peak in north-central Nepal after the avalanche hit on Sunday. The remains of the two people who were killed were airlifted on Monday to Kathmandu airport and transported to the Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital. “Two bodies were found as rescuers worked until 6pm (12:30 GMT) last night,” Tul Singh Gurung, president of the Nepal National Mountain Guide Association, told the AFP news agency. “The search continues for 14 expedition workers who are still missing.” A team of eight mountain guides is involved in the search operation, he added. All those killed or missing were Nepali nationals. The avalanche hit as they were at a base camp preparing for foreign clients to arrive and climb the peak during the autumn climbing season that began this month. #nepal

According to the District Administration Office, the landslide has not completely blocked the Marsyangdi River. However, a large amount of mud has entered the river, increasing the risk of flooding in downstream areas. Assistant Chief District Officer Krishna Prasad Poudel has urged people living along the river and nearby areas to remain highly alert. Authorities have also advised people to avoid unnecessary movement near the riverbanks and stay in safe places. #nepalinlast24hours

Fortes chuvas provocaram enchentes e deslizamentos em Galkot, no distrito de Baglung, no oeste do Nepal, na tarde de domingo (27). Segundo informações divulgadas pelas autoridades locais, ao menos 10 pessoas morreram. Oito casas foram arrastadas em Tamankhola-3, enquanto outros imóveis foram atingidos por deslizamentos em Tamankhola-4 e Nisikhola-3. Entre as vítimas estão quatro integrantes de uma mesma família em Nisikhola. Rodovias e outras estruturas também foram danificadas. Em Tanahun, 24 casas, distribuídas por seis localidades, foram atingidas pelas enchentes e deslizamentos, além de um moinho de arroz e instalações destinadas à criação de animais. A elevação do Rio Kaligandaki também provocou danos na Caverna Sita, em Devghat. Um sacerdote de 76 anos que estava na região afetada foi resgatado pela polícia. The deadly floods in Nepal that brought destruction on 26 August have left the Himalayan nation grappling with heavy losses and mounting reconstruction needs. A month after the catastrophe, helicopters still ferry food and medicine to isolated settlements, where thousands face an uncertain future. The disaster has exposed the risks facing communities living below the world's highest peaks, where even a small increase in global temperatures can destabilise glaciers and river systems. The floods killed more than 1,400 people and left over 6,000 missing in Nepal and China's Tibet region. 🎥 Jalees Andrabi ✍️ Paavan Mathema 💻 Sebastian Evans
